steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Appeasement was the policy of giving in to some of Hitler's demands in the hope of avoiding war. It was most associated with British Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain (1937-1940), though it had been practised by earlier governments. The policy was based on the belief that some of Germany's grievances were legitimate and that negotiated concessions could satisfy Hitler and prevent another devastating war.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Appeasement was not simply cowardice or stupidity. It was a rational policy based on genuine concerns: war weariness, military unpreparedness, economic problems, fear of communism, and the belief that some German grievances were legitimate.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Neville Chamberlain became Prime Minister in May 1937 and made appeasement the cornerstone of British foreign policy. He believed that personal diplomacy could solve international problems and conducted his own negotiations with Hitler, bypassing the Foreign Office.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The strongest argument for appeasement was that it bought time for rearmament. In 1938, Britain had only 5 radar stations and very few Spitfires. By September 1939, the radar chain was complete and the RAF had over 300 Spitfires and Hurricanes. However, Germany also used the time to rearm, so the balance of power may not have changed significantly in Britain's favour.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain two reasons why Britain followed a policy of appeasement. (4 marks) | How far was appeasement justified? (8 marks) | "Appeasement was cowardly and misguided." How far do you agree? (12 marks)

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know the five reasons for appeasement: war weariness, military weakness, economic problems, fear of communism, belief in fairness Chamberlain's "peace for our time" quote (30 September 1938) is essential Always give BALANCED arguments - appeasement had genuine justifications even if it was ultimately wrong The Czech takeover (March 1939) is the turning point when appeasement was abandoned Link appeasement to the wider failures of the League of Nations - they are connected topics The guarantee to Poland (31 March 1939) marked the formal end of appeasement For "was appeasement justified" questions, always consider what the alternatives were at the time
